description: diffing.py implements find_missing(), which reports expected items absent from an actual collection. When nothing is missing it returns None because of a 'result or None' shortcut, forcing callers to special-case the empty result. Fix it so the function always returns a list, preserving the order of ``expected`` and including duplicates that appear in ``expected``.
expected_behavior: find_missing([1, 2, 3], [1, 2, 3]) == []; find_missing(['a', 'b'], ['a']) == ['b']; duplicates in expected are reported individually.
notes: Synthetic defect seeded for the VerifyLoop benchmark. Not a production incident.
title: find_missing returns None instead of an empty list
